title: Longest duplicate substring (length)
statement: Return the length of the longest substring that occurs at least twice in s (occurrences may overlap). n ≤ 3 × 10⁴.
hints: If a length-L duplicate exists, so does a length L − 1 one: binary search on L.
Check a given L in O(n) by hashing every window with a rolling hash.

solution.explanation: Two ideas composed: binary search on the answer (Part 2; the predicate is monotone) and a rolling (Rabin–Karp) hash that updates a window's hash in O(1). Hash collisions are possible: use a large modulus (2⁶¹ − 1) and verify candidate matches, or two independent hashes. A suffix array gives a deterministic O(n log n) solution, worth mentioning.
